title: Latin Empire
capsule: The crusader state installed in Constantinople after the Fourth Crusade (1204), with Baldwin of Flanders as emperor and Venice as chief beneficiary. Never secure beyond the capital’s hinterland, it fell to the Nicaean Greeks in 1261.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases (Times Atlas of World History; Kinder & Hilgemann; Shepherd 1926) at ~0.07° resolution. Thracian core attested; Greek lordships nominally subject are drawn separately. Confidence: moderate.

citations.label: Setton (ed.), A History of the Crusades, vol. II (U. Wisconsin; free online)
